newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela delays Cristobal gas project up to 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela delays Cristobal gas project up to 5 yrs.

text.p: Venezuela's Energy and Mines Ministry and state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) will decide Monday to put off the massive Cristobal Colon natural gas project in Venezuela "for up to five years", a top government official said.
Evanan Romero, vice-minister of Energy and Mines said the project was being delayed because the price of natural gas did not justify the multi-billion dollar investment required.
"We cannot go against the market," Romero told reporters in Congress.

The Cristobal Colon project is being developed by Sucre Gas SA, a joint venture between Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) unit Lagoven (33 percent), Royal Dutch Shell (30 percent), Exxon Corp (29 percent) and Mitsubishi Corp (eight percent).
"They are talking about suspending the project for up to five years to see whether in this time the bubble between supply and demand for gas disappears," he said.
The project, located off Venezuela's northeastern Caribbean coast, was initially budgeted to require investment of $5.4 billion although low gas prices have seen the project scaled down subsequently.
PDVSA President Luis Giusti said that the Sucre Gas partners had until Dec 31 to make a final decision on whether to go ahead with the project.
"The probability is that it will be postponed but we do not know for how long," he said.
Giusti stressed that the project's partners were still interested in continuing with the project but might have to wait some time before doing so.
"All projects must have an economic reason to proceed of at least a 10 percent rate of return in real terms. If not, the project is not done, no matter how much interest there is," he added.
